summary:
FireWatch – Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hotspots.

Firewatch is a satellite-based fire monitoring and geospatial analysis system developed to address the challenge of harmonizing active fire hotspot observations from MODIS and VIIRS satellite instruments. It brings together observations from MODIS, NOAA-20 VIIRS and NOAA-21 VIIRS into a unified analytical platform, enabling consistent exploration and comparison of fire activity across South Asia. The system organizes satellite observations using common geographic, temporal and fire-related parameters, helping users examine hotspot distribution, compare satellite detections, analyze Fire Radiative Power (FRP) and understand detection confidence. Through interactive geospatial visualization and hotspot-density analysis, FireWatch transforms multiple satellite datasets into meaningful and accessible information.
By improving the accessibility and comparative interpretation of satellite fire observations, FireWatch supports better understanding of regional fire activity and can contribute to environmental monitoring, research and informed decision-making.

FIREWATCH

Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots

NASA Space Apps Challenge – Project Details

1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

FireWatch is a satellite-based fire monitoring and geospatial analysis platform designed to bring together fire hotspot observations from multiple satellite sources into one interactive dashboard.

It combines observations from NASA MODIS, NOAA-20 VIIRS and NOAA-21 VIIRS, allowing users to explore, compare and understand fire activity across South Asia through maps, visual analytics and geographic summaries.

2. PROBLEM STATEMENT

Fire observations are collected by different satellite instruments, and their datasets are often available separately. This makes it challenging to compare satellite observations, understand the geographical distribution of hotspots, analyze fire intensity and interpret large datasets efficiently.

FireWatch addresses this challenge by organizing multiple satellite observations into a common analytical platform.

3. HOW FIREWATCH WORKS

Step 1: Satellite Data Collection

FireWatch uses satellite fire observation datasets obtained from NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System).

The three datasets used are:

  • MODIS C6.1 – South Asia
  • VIIRS NOAA-20 – South Asia
  • VIIRS NOAA-21 – South Asia

These datasets contain information such as latitude, longitude, observation date and time, brightness temperature, Fire Radiative Power (FRP) and detection confidence.

Step 2: Data Processing

The datasets are loaded and processed using Python and Pandas. Important columns and formats are standardized, satellite sources are identified, and observations are combined into a common dataset for further analysis.

Step 3: Geospatial and Statistical Analysis

The processed observations are analyzed based on geographic location, observation time, fire intensity, detection confidence and hotspot density.

Step 4: Interactive Dashboard

The results are displayed through an interactive dashboard where users can filter observations and explore maps, charts, comparisons and regional summaries.

Note: The current prototype uses downloaded NASA FIRMS CSV snapshots. Automatic near-real-time data integration is planned for a future version.

4. CORE FEATURES

A. Geospatial Hotspot Mapping

Displays detected hotspot locations on an interactive map to help users understand their geographic distribution and identify areas with concentrated fire observations.

B. Fire Activity Timeline

Displays daily observation trends to explore changes in detected fire activity over the selected observation period.

C. Multi-Satellite Comparison

Compares observations from MODIS, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 in one analytical environment. Users can examine satellite-wise observation counts and FRP statistics.

D. Fire Radiative Power (FRP) Analysis

Examines Fire Radiative Power values to understand the intensity characteristics of observed fires. The dashboard displays average, minimum and maximum FRP and intensity distributions.

The project uses the following FRP categories:

  • Low: Below 20 MW
  • Moderate: 20–50 MW
  • High: Above 50 MW

E. Detection Confidence Analysis

Displays confidence information associated with satellite fire detections, helping users inspect the confidence characteristics of the observations.

F. Geographic Density Analysis

Groups observations into geographic grid cells and highlights areas with higher, moderate and lower hotspot concentrations. These are observation-density indicators, not predictions of future fires.

G. Multi-Satellite Grid Analysis

Uses rounded geographic coordinates to identify grid cells containing observations from multiple satellite sources. This provides a common spatial framework for examining overlapping satellite observations.

H. Country-Wise Activity Analysis

Provides regional summaries for countries across South Asia, including hotspot observations and FRP statistics. The current country grouping uses approximate geographic coordinate boundaries.

I. Fire Detection Records

Displays individual satellite observation records, including observation time, satellite source, latitude, longitude, brightness, FRP and confidence.

5. TECHNOLOGY STACK

  • Python: Main programming language used for application logic and data processing.
  • Pandas: Used to load, clean, standardize and combine satellite datasets.
  • NumPy: Used for numerical and array operations.
  • Streamlit: Used to develop the interactive web dashboard.
  • Folium: Used for interactive geographic mapping and hotspot visualization.
  • Matplotlib: Used to create charts and statistical visualizations.
  • Requests: Used for HTTP requests and potential future data integration.
  • NASA FIRMS: Source of satellite fire observation datasets.
  • Visual Studio Code: Development environment used to build the project.

6. WHAT MAKES FIREWATCH CREATIVE?

FireWatch goes beyond displaying individual fire locations. It brings multiple satellite datasets into one analytical environment and provides different ways to investigate the observations.

Its creative contributions include:

  1. Unified Satellite Analysis: Combines MODIS, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 observations into one platform.
  2. Spatial Intelligence: Uses geographic grid analysis to examine hotspot concentrations.
  3. Comparative Visualization: Provides satellite-wise statistics and FRP comparisons.
